Thanks for the ping and the logs — looked through the GOV logs and infra metrics. Quick summary:

- Root cause (short): a recent config rollout (specterx-serving v1.14.3) enabled a more aggressive KV-cache eviction heuristic for short-lived sessions. Under the bursty pattern we see from Acme's workflow, the new heuristic increases cache churn which causes repeated backend recomputation and queuing on the SpecterX model shards. That leads to queue saturation and downstream 5xx/timeouts.

- Evidence: increased cache-miss rate correlated with request queue growth between 06:40-07:10 PDT; sample server traces (server_id=usw-12a) show repeated full-decode work loops for nearly-identical prefixes.

Immediate actions taken (08:00 PDT):
1) Rolled back the KV eviction heuristic to v1.14.2 for the US-west serving pool (expected to reduce churn).
2) Opened automated routing to SpecterX-6b-psi (a compatible quantized variant) for clients with latency SLOs — opt-in per-customer for now.
3) Increased short-term concurrency on the affected shards to reduce queue head-of-line blocking.

Current status: error rates down from ~18% to ~4% in the affected pool since the rollback, and we are monitoring for stabilization. We will keep Acme routed to SpecterX-6b-psi if they opt-in; otherwise we expect full recovery on production within 30–45 minutes as caches warm.

Next steps:
- Rafael: please capture the config diff and open a postmortem ticket with timeline and fix plan (config gating + canary target criteria).
- Jonas: coordinate any commercial remedy (service credit) and confirm with Laura on wording.

Ben
